## GET /admin-api/claim-providers

`getClaimProviders`

**The Claims Providers this realm aggregates claims from, and every person's link (OIDC Core 5.6.2)**

Everything /admin/claim-providers draws: each registered provider (issuer, endpoints, client, the claims it supplies, aggregated or distributed, whether a secret is held), the redirect URI to register at a provider, and every link a person made (their subject there, when, the token's expiry, whether it is stale). Never a secret or a token.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/claim-providers` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `providersPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the providers. Clamped, like every page parameter here. |
| `linkq` | query | string |  | Narrows the links to those whose person, provider or subject there contains this. |
| `linksPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the matched links. It shares `per` with the providers. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page of each list, capped. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## POST /admin-api/claim-providers/add-provider

`addClaimProvider`

**Register a Claims Provider**

A provider this realm aggregates claims from. `discover` fills the endpoints left empty from the issuer's discovery document; the secret is sealed. Audited.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/claim-providers` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

|---|---|---|---|---|

| `clientId` | string | yes | This realm's client_id at the provider. |
| `clientSecret` | string |  | Sealed where keys persist; never returned. |
| `delivery` | one of `aggregated`, `distributed` |  |  |
| `discover` | boolean |  | Fill the endpoints left empty from the issuer's discovery document. |

## GET /admin-api/commands

`getProviderCommands`

**OpenID Provider Commands: the clients, the account register, the tenant runs and the deliveries**

Everything /admin/commands draws: whether commands and automatic commands are on, the issuer Command Tokens name, each client with a command_endpoint and what its metadata answer said it supports, the account-state register (what each relying party said about each person), the tenant runs, and the command deliveries. `state` and `q` narrow the deliveries. Never a token.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/commands` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clientsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `clients`. Each list moves on its own parameter and they share `per`. |
| `accountsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `accounts`. Each list moves on its own parameter and they share `per`. |
| `runsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `runs`. Each list moves on its own parameter and they share `per`. |
| `deliveriesPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `deliveries`. Each list moves on its own parameter and they share `per`. |
| `state` | query | string |  | Only deliveries in this state: pending, sent or dead. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Narrows the deliveries. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page of each list, capped. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## GET /admin-api/oauth2

`getOauth2Settings`

**The authorization server's own settings**

The `oauth2.*` settings: the issuer identifier, RFC 9700 mode, OAuth 2.1 mode (`oauth2.oauth21`, draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-16, which implies RFC 9700 mode), the registered redirect URIs and the loopback port wildcard, Front-Channel Logout, the refresh token idle timeout, whether a sign-out revokes refresh tokens, the client assertion clock skew, the four lifetimes `GET /token-lifetimes` also reports — and `oauth2.breakIdTokenNonce`, which makes this service return an ID Token whose `nonce` is WRONG so that a client can be shown to check it — in development mode only; a product realm ignores it and refuses setting it.

`oauth2.rfc9700` is restart-only and says so in `restartReason`: `global.https` derives from it and a listener's scheme is settled when the socket is bound. A TRUST REALM can carry it while the process does not, which is how one process answers permissively at /oauth2/authorize and enforces the BCP under a realm prefix.

THERE IS NO POST BESIDE THIS ONE and that is not a gap: every form on the console page this mirrors posts `set-many` to /admin/config, so `POST /admin-api/config/set-many` is already the operation for it. One store, one action, two doors.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/oauth2` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

`getOauth2Monitor`

**What the authorization server has done in this realm, by mechanism, with the pushed authorization requests still held**

Everything /admin/oauth2/monitor draws, in SECTIONS — one per mechanism counted, RFC 9126 pushed authorization requests the first. Each section carries its events (the closed vocabulary with a label and a total each), the totals, the OAuth errors returned, one row per client_id with every counter (paged by `clientsPage` and `per`), and — for RFC 9126 — the pushed requests the store still holds, newest first: the digest of the request_uri (its handle; the request_uri itself is not kept), client, authorization server, state, created and expiry, reads, whether and how the client authenticated, form or request object, the redirect_uri and whether section 2.4 let it in unregistered, the DPoP key, and the parameters. That list is paged by `offset` and `limit` (or the console's `page` and `per`) and filtered by `state` and `client_id`. RFC 9470's step-up is the second section (`stepup`), its clients paged by `stepUpClientsPage`, carrying the requirement this service's own resource server enforces (`ownResourceRequirement`) and `acrValuesSupported`. Per trust realm, merged across processes, and with no reset.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/oauth2/monitor` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `offset` | query | integer |  | Skip this many pushed requests (newest first). Wins over `page` when both are sent. |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | At most this many pushed requests; 50 by default. |
| `state` | query | one of `live`, `spent`, `all` |  | `live` (not yet spent), `spent` (an authorization response was issued on it; kept until it would have expired), or `all`, the default. |
| `client_id` | query | string |  | Only the pushed requests bound to this client. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | The console's spelling: which page of pushed requests, `per` to a page. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page, for `page` and `clientsPage`. |
| `clientsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the RFC 9126 section's per-client counter rows. |
| `stepUpClientsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the RFC 9470 section's per-client counter rows. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## POST /admin-api/oauth2/monitor/delete-pushed-request

`deletePushedRequest`

**Withdraw a pushed authorization request (RFC 9126)**

Removes one pushed request, named by the SHA-256 of its request_uri, from this realm's store of pushed authorization requests, live or spent. The authorization endpoint refuses it from then on with 400 invalid_request_uri, exactly as it refuses one that expired and was swept; a browser already on the sign-in or consent screen with it is refused when it comes back. Counted as `par.deleted` and written to the audit log. A value that is not a handle (43 characters of base64url), or one this realm does not hold, is refused 400. The store keeps no request_uri (#614), so the handle is the only name it answers to.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/oauth2/monitor` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `request_uri_digest` | string | yes | The request's handle: the base64url SHA-256 of its whole request_uri, as listed by GET /admin-api/oauth2/monitor. |

**200**: The handle withdrawn, the client it was bound to and the state it was in.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |

| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `request_uri_digest` | string |  |  |
| `state` | string |  |  |
